newsitem.title: UK: Guinness rejects reports of brand divestment.
newsitem.headline: Guinness rejects reports of brand divestment.

text.p: British drinks group Guinness Plc has no plans to streamline brands as a result of its proposed merger with Grand Metropolitian Plc, a spokesman for the company said on Sunday.
"There are no plans to streamline any brands...no secret plans to divest," he said.

Newspaper reports on Sunday had speculated that the merged group, to be called GMG Brands, would either decide to ditch some of its combined spirits portfolio in order to ease marketing or would shed brands to pacify regulators.

"We are confident that we can properly explain to regulators ... that the proposed merger does not bring competition or regulatory problems. So (the reports) are all speculation and we would not comment," the spokesman said.
Guinness and Grand Met unveiled the $15.8 billion merger on May 12.
It will create the world's leading spirits and wine company and the group will be the world's seventh largest branded food and drinks concern.

Guinness Chairman Tony Greener told shareholders at the annual meeting on May 15 that "the range of brands are highly complementary," adding that both groups had remarkably different brands with very few overlaps.
